1773598.title: Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt. Ltd. vs State Of Haryana & Anr
1773598.doc:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (C) NO. 13917 OF 2009

SURAJ LAMP & INDUSTRIES PVT. LTD. ... PETITIONER
vs.
STATE OF HARYANA & ANR. ... RESPONDENTS

JUDGMENT

R.V. RAVEENDRAN, J.

1. This three-Judge Bench was constituted to consider the question whether immovable property can be validly transferred by way of Sale Agreement (SA)/General Power of Attorney (GPA)/Will (WILL) transactions, in lieu of registered deeds of conveyance.

2. We have held that a transfer of immovable property by way of SA/GPA/WILL transactions does not convey title and does not amount to transfer, nor can it be recognized as a valid mode of transfer of immovable property. The courts will not treat such transactions as completed or concluded transfers or as conveyances as they neither convey title nor create any interest in an immovable property.

3. Sections 17 and 49 of the Registration Act, 1908 and Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 mandate that a transfer of immovable property of value exceeding Rs. 100 can be made only by a registered instrument...

1846896.title: Saraswathamma vs H. Sharad Shrikhande And Ors
1846896.doc:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO. 9215 OF 2014

SARASWATHAMMA ... APPELLANT
vs.
H. SHARAD SHRIKHANDE & ORS. ... RESPONDENTS

JUDGMENT

1. This appeal arises out of a suit for specific performance of an agreement to sell dated 12.04.1991 in respect of immovable property.

2. Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 mandates that the plaintiff must aver and prove continuous readiness and willingness from the date of the agreement until the date of decree.

3. The mere filing of the suit within the period of limitation does not by itself establish readiness and willingness. The plaintiff must demonstrate financial capacity, conduct showing willingness to perform, and absence of conduct showing repudiation.

4. As regards the question of time being the essence of contract in agreements for sale of immovable property, the settled position is that time is generally not the essence of the contract, unless specifically made so by express stipulation...

1320963.title: Anathula Sudhakar vs P. Buchi Reddy (Dead) By Lrs. & Ors
1320963.doc:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

CIVIL APPEAL NO. 6191 OF 2001

ANATHULA SUDHAKAR ... APPELLANT
vs.
P. BUCHI REDDY (DEAD) BY LRS. & ORS. ... RESPONDENTS

JUDGMENT

R.V. RAVEENDRAN, J.

1. The question that arises in this appeal is whether in a suit for permanent injunction restraining the defendant from interfering with the plaintiff's possession, the plaintiff is required to seek declaration of title also.

2. We summarize the legal position as follows:
   (a) Where a plaintiff is in lawful or peaceful possession of a property and such possession is interfered with by the defendant, a suit for permanent injunction simpliciter is maintainable.
   (b) Where the title of the plaintiff is in dispute or under cloud, a suit for declaration of title coupled with consequential relief of injunction is the proper remedy.
   (c) Where the plaintiff is not in possession, he has to seek the relief of possession with or without declaration of title.

3. The factors that determine when declaration is necessary include: whether title is denied, whether title is under cloud, and whether plaintiff is in possession...

1428104.title: Sopan Sukhdeo Sable & Ors vs Asstt. Charity Commissioner & Ors
1428104.doc:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

CIVIL APPEAL NO. 2735 OF 2004

SOPAN SUKHDEO SABLE & ORS. ... APPELLANTS
vs.
ASSTT. CHARITY COMMISSIONER & ORS. ... RESPONDENTS

JUDGMENT

ARIJIT PASAYAT, J.

1. The question before us concerns the scope of Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — the power of the court to reject a plaint.

2. The provisions of Order VII Rule 11 are mandatory. The court must consider the averments in the plaint as they stand, without addition or subtraction.

3. The plaint must be read as a whole. It is not permissible for the court to dissect the pleadings into several parts and to consider whether each part discloses a cause of action separately. If on a meaningful reading of the plaint, it discloses a cause of action, then the plaint cannot be rejected.

4. A clever drafting which creates the illusion of a cause of action where none exists is a different matter and the court is duty bound to nip such matters in the bud...

199352.title: Vidhyadhar vs Manikrao & Anr
199352.doc:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

CIVIL APPEAL NO. 1432 OF 1999

VIDHYADHAR ... APPELLANT
vs.
MANIKRAO & ANR. ... RESPONDENTS

JUDGMENT

SAGHIR AHMAD, J.

1. This appeal raises a significant question regarding the evidentiary value of a party's failure to appear as a witness in support of his own case.

2. Section 114 illustration (g) of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 provides that the court may presume that evidence which could be and is not produced would, if produced, be unfavourable to the person who withholds it.

3. Where a party to a suit does not appear in the witness box and states his own case on oath, and does not offer himself to be cross-examined by the other side, a presumption would arise that the case set up by him is not correct.

4. This principle has been applied consistently in civil litigation, particularly in suits involving questions of title, possession, fraud, and breach of contract where personal knowledge of the party is material...
